title: What Portfolio Should You Look For in a Westchester Architect
excerpt: Choosing the right architect for your Westchester home means looking at real work they've done in your own backyard. Here's what matters most.
content:
When you're planning a home renovation or addition in Westchester, you'll eventually need to find an architect. The question most homeowners ask is simple: how do I know if this person is actually good at what they do?

The answer is in their portfolio. Not the polished photos on a website, but the real homes they've worked on. Homes in towns you recognize. Projects that solve problems similar to yours.

Look for Work in Your Town (and Towns Like Yours)

A licensed architect in Westchester, NY who has completed projects in your specific community understands your local building department and your neighbors' homes. They know what fits. They know what doesn't. If you live in Scarsdale, look for a residential architect in Scarsdale who has navigated your town's approval process before. If you're in Mamaroneck or Larchmont, the same principle applies.

Experience matters because every Westchester municipality has its own building department and permit process. An architect familiar with your town's requirements, design guidelines, and review standards will move your project forward more smoothly. They've done this work before. They know the people involved.

This doesn't mean your architect has to live in your town. A licensed architect based in Eastchester can work effectively in Bronxville, Rye, or Harrison. What matters is that their portfolio shows they've completed successful projects across the communities you're considering.

Does Their Work Match Your Project Type?

Not all architects are equally skilled in all project types. Some focus heavily on new construction. Others excel at historic restorations. A few understand both kitchen remodeling and second-story additions with equal competence.

When you look at a portfolio, ask yourself whether you see work similar to what you need. If you want an open-concept conversion, find evidence they've done that. If you're adding a primary suite, look for projects where that was the goal. Home additions in Westchester come in many forms, and your architect should have hands-on experience with your specific type.

The strongest portfolios show range. A single architect handling home renovations, kitchen remodels, bathroom updates, and custom additions tells you they understand residential design across multiple contexts.

Design-Build Credentials Change Everything

Here's something worth paying attention to: is your architect also a licensed general contractor? This matters more than most homeowners realize.

A design-build firm in Westchester means one person understands both the design vision and the actual construction. They're not handing off your project to someone else halfway through. When an architect who is also a general contractor designs your home, they're thinking about buildability from day one. They know what costs time. They know what saves money. They catch problems before they become expensive.

Look for portfolios where the same person who designed the project also oversaw its construction. That accountability shows up in the final result.
